extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy (metaphysics, philosophy of time) and history/philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and assessing the standards by which scientific and metaphysical accounts of time, duration, and becoming are judged in Bergson's Creative Evolution. Includes criteria for what counts as adequate science, metaphysics, and artistic/psychical accounts of duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern science defined by taking time as independent variable
rubrics_metrics.description: "modern science must be defined pre-eminently by its aspiration to take time as an independent variable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson treats this as a defining aspiration: modern laws relate magnitudes to time (e.g., Kepler, Galileo). The scientific project makes time the magnitude to which others are related, using time as a uniform, chosen representative (the mobile T) whose divisions index events. This is the criterion by which an account is 'scientific' in the modern sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the cinematographical method (counting simultaneities, isolating instants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive science 'counts simultaneities' and retains only positions (points) on chosen trajectories, never the flux itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science abstracts time by sampling virtual 'stops' (T1, T2, ...), comparing simultaneous positions of systems; it does not register the flowing flux of duration. Any account that reduces temporal processes to a series of instants or to numerable correspondences exemplifies this cinematographical method and is limited thereby.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physics substitutes time-length for time-invention
rubrics_metrics.description: "while modern physics ... rests altogether on a substitution of time-length for time-invention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson criticizes physics for reducing the qualitative, inventive aspect of temporal becoming to measurable lengths (numbers of units). Evaluations should check whether a theory merely measures durations (time-length) or accounts for creative, qualitative becoming (time-invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy requires accounting for the flux (duration) not only instants
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific knowledge 'retains only the events or systems of events that can be thus isolated' and therefore misses the 'flux of time' and 'its effect on consciousness'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A metaphysical or psychological account is judged better insofar as it attempts to follow the flow of time itself (duration), not merely its discretized views. Bergson suggests a complementary faculty (intuition) is needed to grasp real duration that intellect/science leaves out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hypostatizing methodological rules into metaphysical doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodological rule to act 'as if' a tool's applicability were unlimited was sometimes turned into 'a fundamental law of things' (universal mechanism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson treats it as a mistake to convert a practical research rule (proceed as if physics were universally applicable) into an ontological claim about the universe. Criteria for metaphysical rigor include distinguishing method from metaphysical claim and not elevating a research heuristic to ultimate reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism should be a method, not an absolute doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism, properly, can 'become a method rather than a doctrine'—a way science scans the flow of things rather than a statement that all is mechanistically determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mechanistic explanations by whether they are presented as instrumental (limited, local, methodological) or as universal, metaphysical theses. Preference is given to positions that keep mechanism as a productive method without denying creative duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject metaphysics that concludes 'All is given' (denial of creative succession)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophies that compress laws/concepts into a unity end with the immanent conclusion: 'All is given.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson sees as an error any metaphysics whose immanent logic implies the whole of reality is exhaustively present (eternally given) and thus denies genuine creation and open future. A satisfactory metaphysics must allow for an undetermined future and real succession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscious/psychical duration is qualitative and absolute for consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: For consciousness the duration of a phenomenon is an 'absolute' coinciding with a 'degree of impatience' and not reducible to relative numbered units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing accounts of temporal experience (psychology, aesthetics), one should test whether they capture the qualitative, felt length of durations (e.g., waiting for sugar to dissolve) rather than only measurable temporal units. The felt, qualitative aspect has normative significance for theories of mind and art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-invention is essential to creativity/art: duration is part of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: "The time taken up by the invention, is one with the invention itself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating artistic or creative processes, Bergson treats temporal unfolding as integral to the work's essence. Compressing or dilating the creative time would alter the psychical evolution and the invention; thus quality of creative output depends on its temporal mode of genesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty arises from internal impetus in duration (continuous creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelty of works (and of nature) 'arises from an internal impetus which is progress or succession', and the 'duration of the universe must therefore be one with the latitude of creation which can find place in it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A metaphysical account earns adequacy if it allows for continuous growth and genuine novelty produced within duration, not merely the rearrangement of pre-existing eternal elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of cutting reality into quantity and quality (the scission critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new science 'cut the real into two halves, quantity and quality', leading to an irreparable scission between body and soul and to syntheses that embrace only one half.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should check whether a theory illegitimately privileges quantitative (measurable) aspects and neglects qualitative perception and lived experience. A robust account should avoid reducing perceptual/psychical content to purely quantitative terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rule to act 'as if' instruments are unlimited (practical but fallible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the new science only had hold of certain systems, it was 'useful to proceed always and everywhere as if the condition was realized'—a natural methodological rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson recognizes the pragmatic rationality of treating tools as broadly applicable when their limits are unknown, but warns this is a methodological convenience, not proof of metaphysical completeness. Critical scrutiny should distinguish warranted methodological extension from unwarranted metaphysical generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: A satisfactory metaphysics must supplement intellect with intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: To hold true duration 'we may open a perspective on the other half of the real... To intellect, in short, there will be added intuition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson proposes that to grasp becoming and creative duration metaphysics needs an intuitive faculty complementary to analytical/intellectual methods. Thus criterion for metaphysical adequacy includes whether it incorporates or allows for such an intuitive grasp of duration.
